therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: PD-1 checkpoint inhibition combined with microbiome modulation to enhance immune response
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: T-cell activation and anti-tumor immunity enhancement through checkpoint blockade and microbiome-mediated immune stimulation
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Patients with advanced or metastatic melanoma, gastric cancer, gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma, and colorectal cancer
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Safety and tolerability, and objective response rate

results.effect_size: ORR: 1/56 total patients (1.8%), 1/21 gastric patients (4.8%), 0/21 melanoma patients, 0/14 colorectal patients
results.target_engagement_evidence: VE800 bacterial strain colonization detected in stool samples
biomarker_changes: VE800 bacterial strain colonization in stool
subgroup_findings: Only gastric cancer patients showed objective response (1/21, 4.8%)
Disease control rate: gastric 3/21 (14.3%), melanoma 9/21 (42.9%), colorectal 3/14 (21.4%)
Median PFS similar across tumor types: 1.8-1.9 months
results.dose_information: VE800 orally administered live biotherapeutic product with nivolumab, vancomycin pretreatment used

context.duration: Up to 56.7 weeks treatment, 18 months follow-up
